text: Handwara is a town in the Kupwara district of Jammu and Kashmir, India, situated on the Baramulla-Handwara National Highway NH-701 and governed by a Municipal Committee comprising 13 elected members. Located at 34°24′N 74°17′E (34.40°N 74.28°E) at an average elevation of 1,582 metres (5,190 feet) above sea level, the town is surrounded by natural beauty, including the Pohru River (locally known as the Talri river), a tributary of the Jhelum. During Sikh rule, Raja Zabardast Khan, chieftain of the Bomba tribe, led guerrilla warfare against the Sikh Empire, attacking their garrisons and posts in Handwara. A prominent volcanic peak named Soyamji (1860 metres), locally known as Paput, lies in North Machhipura (Handwara) and is recognized for its unique conical shape; it experienced a lava eruption lasting about 13 months in 1934 and has remained dormant since. According to the 2011 Indian census, Handwara has a population of 13,600, with males making up 54.26% and females 45.74% of the population. The town's average literacy rate is 64.39%, which is below the national average of 67.16%, with male literacy at 75.62% and female literacy at 51.88%. Islam is the dominant religion in Handwara. The region holds significant strategic importance due to its proximity to the Line of Control (LoC), making it a critical and sensitive area in military and security contexts. Handwara was the home constituency of the late separatist leader Abdul Ghani Lone. The current MLA of Handwara is Sajjad Gani Lone of the Jammu and Kashmir People's Conference, who won the 2024 assembly elections by over 600 votes against Chowdhary Mohammad Ramzaan of the Jammu & Kashmir National Conference.
